mappings.note: Track the bean plant from sowing to pod, recording dated observations AND sketches. LO-108 for the sustained investigation, LO-112 because the sketch column is required work.
Sort pencil, book, pigeon, car and plant into living and non-living WITH a reason each. Classifying on observable properties, LO-107.
Predict, then observe germination across four pots differing in water, air and light. A controlled investigation with predictions recorded, LO-108.
Predict and observe root and shoot direction in three beaker set-ups, including an inverted plant. A controlled investigation, LO-108.
Design an activity to decide which of larva and pupa leads to the other, WITHOUT separating them. Planning an investigation under a constraint, LO-108.
Which characteristics set living beings apart from non-living things. An explicit differentiation of the two on their properties, LO-106.
Avadhi's mother stops her taking a shell that may house a living snail. Care for living things and their habitat, LO-115.
Why a car counts as non-living although it moves. Requires holding the living/non-living distinction against a hard case, LO-106.
What a stimulus is. Naming the concept, LO-105; nothing is compared or sorted.
Touch-me-not folds its leaves when touched. LO-110 names 'movements in plants and animals' as its own example.
Why living beings reproduce -- continuity of the species. Explaining a life process, LO-110.
What excretion is. Explaining a life process, LO-110.
The leaf pores for gas exchange are stomata. Naming a structure, LO-105.
How plant movement differs from animal movement. An explicit differentiation, LO-106, where the touch-me-not item was the movement itself and got LO-110.
Which single condition is under test when only light is varied between two pots. Recognising the design of a controlled investigation, LO-108.
The conditions bean seeds actually need -- the right amount of water and air. The conclusion of the germination investigation, LO-108.
The seed's outer covering is the seed coat. Naming a structure, LO-105.
What germination means. Explaining a life process, LO-110.
An inverted seedling reorients -- shoot up, root down. Explaining a growth movement, LO-110.
J.C. Bose built the crescograph to record plant responses. Constructing an instrument and what it shows, LO-113; no LO covers scientists' lives, and his contribution was the device.
What a plant's life cycle is, seed to seed. Explaining a process, LO-110.
Recognising the described sequence as a complete bean life cycle. Explaining a process from an account of it, LO-110.
The worm-like stages in stagnant water are larva and pupa. Identifying organisms' stages by appearance and where they occur, LO-105.
Why standing water must not be allowed to collect -- it breeds mosquitoes. A protective habit for the surroundings, LO-115.
The key difference between larval and pupal stages in shape and appearance. An explicit differentiation, LO-106.
Which is NOT one of the mosquito's four stages -- nymph. Tests the boundary of the life-cycle stage set, LO-107.
Assertion-reason: kerosene works BECAUSE the film blocks larvae from breathing. The causal clause is what is marked, LO-109.

Which statements about growth, reproduction and stimulus response distinguish living from non-living. Differentiating the two on their properties, LO-106. Only the last of the three numbered statements survives in the stem.
Why waterlogged pots germinate poorly -- excess water excludes air. The cause behind an observed failure, LO-109.
The jelly-like cluster of frog eggs is spawn. Naming a stage from its appearance, LO-105.
Why tadpoles have tails -- to swim in their aquatic stage. A structure related to the demand of its habitat, LO-109.
What a froglet is -- legs grown, tail still present. Identifying a stage by its observable features, LO-105.
How the adult frog's habitat differs from the tadpole's. An explicit differentiation of two stages, LO-106.
Which is NOT true of Drosera -- it does not live on soil nutrients alone. Identification of an organism by its distinguishing features, LO-105. The plant's name is corrupted to 'Drovers' in the stem.
Where to look for mosquito larvae and pupae. Planning where to collect specimens for observation, LO-108.
Assertion-reason: plants grow BECAUSE nutrition supplies what growth needs. The causal clause is what is marked, LO-109.

Which germination statements hold -- water and air yes, sunlight no, excess water harmful. The conclusions of the germination investigation, LO-108. Only the last of the three numbered statements survives in the stem.
Drosera's hairs closing on an insect as a response to stimulus. LO-110's 'movements in plants' example.
The silk moth also passes through four stages. Placing a second insect in the same life-cycle classification, LO-107.
Why the first phase is called germination rather than growth. Explaining what distinguishes the process, LO-110.
Ceasing to show life characteristics despite resources is death. Explaining a life process, LO-110.
The root grows down into the soil. Naming a part by what it does, LO-105.
How a mosquito larva's habitat differs from the adult's. An explicit differentiation of two stages, LO-106.
Which is NOT an essential germination condition -- sunlight. The conclusion of the germination investigation, LO-108.
A shoot bending towards a window is a response to light. Explaining a growth movement, LO-110.
Why waterlogged soil defeats germination -- no oxygen for respiration. The cause behind a failure, LO-109.
The plumule of the embryo becomes the shoot. Naming a seed part by what it becomes, LO-105.
An adult mosquito lives about 10 to 15 days. A quantity attached to a life stage, LO-111; the frame's measurement outcome is the only one that reaches a duration.
How a mosquito larva looks against the adult. An explicit differentiation of two stages, LO-106.
Which feature the mosquito and silk moth do NOT share -- aquatic adults. Tests the boundary of a shared life-cycle classification, LO-107.
Hind legs with a tail still present identifies a late tadpole or froglet. Identifying a stage from observable features, LO-105.
Assertion-reason: living beings need food BECAUSE it supplies energy for growth and function. The causal clause is what is marked, LO-109.

Which conditions germination requires -- water, air and a suitable temperature, not constant bright sun. The conclusions of the investigation, LO-108. Only the last of the three numbered conditions survives in the stem.
Amla leaves closing at night and opening by day as a response to light. LO-110's 'movements in plants' example.
Producing new individuals of one's own kind is reproduction. Explaining a life process, LO-110.
A shoot growing up responds to gravity and to light at once. Explaining a growth movement and its two stimuli, LO-110.
The embryo is the tiny undeveloped plant inside the seed. Naming a structure, LO-105.
Which stage follows the legged tadpole -- the froglet. Ordering the life-cycle stage set, LO-107.
How animal respiration differs from plant gas exchange -- lungs or gills against stomata. An explicit differentiation on structure, LO-106.
Which is NOT true of the pupal stage -- it does not fly or feed. Identifying a stage by its features, LO-105.
